sites.name: IM-1 Odysseus landing site (Malapert A)
sites.label: IM-1 Odysseus
sites.blurb: Where the Odysseus lander touched down in February 2024
sites.mission_end_source: Intuitive Machines, IM-1 mission update 29 Feb 2024: final transmission as the lunar night began (hour not published; 00:00 UTC used)
sites.mission_note: Odysseus tipped onto its side at touchdown, with its panels tilted away from the low Sun; power ran out about three days before the predicted sunset.
sites.source: NASA / Intuitive Machines, February 2024

sites.name: IM-2 Athena landing site (Mons Mouton)
sites.label: IM-2 Athena
sites.blurb: Where the Athena lander came to rest on its side in March 2025
sites.mission_end_source: Intuitive Machines / NASA release 7 Mar 2025: mission concluded, batteries depleted (hour not published; 12:00 UTC used)
sites.mission_note: Athena came to rest on its side in a crater with the Sun barely above the hills; its batteries drained within a day, with about twelve days of daylight left.
sites.source: Intuitive Machines / LROC, March 2025

sites.name: Blue Ghost Mission 1 landing site (Mare Crisium)
sites.label: Blue Ghost Mission 1
sites.blurb: Where Blue Ghost worked for 14 days in March 2025, far from the pole
sites.mission_end_source: Firefly Aerospace, Blue Ghost Mission 1 update 16 Mar 2025: mission concluded at 23:25 UTC, about 5 h after lunar sunset
sites.mission_note: Blue Ghost worked through the whole lunar day on the flat plain of Mare Crisium and fell silent about 5 hours after the sunset it saw. Our sunset, worked out for a flat horizon, comes about 2.5 hours after the one it saw, so its last signal came 2.4 hours after ours.
sites.source: Firefly Aerospace / NSSDCA, March 2025

sites.name: IM-3 landing target (Reiner Gamma)
sites.label: IM-3 Reiner Gamma
sites.blurb: Where Intuitive Machines' third lander is to land, on a bright swirl
sites.source: NASA CLPS task order CP-11 (Intuitive Machines IM-3, Reiner Gamma); target 7.585°N, 58.725°W from Blewett et al., LPSC 2023 abstract 1780 (NASA NTRS 20230000531)

sites.name: CP-12 landing region (Schrödinger basin, far side)
sites.label: CP-12 Schrödinger
sites.blurb: Where Draper's mission is to land, in a far side basin near the pole
sites.source: NASA CLPS task order CP-12 (Draper, ispace-U.S. APEX 1.0 lander, Schrödinger basin); basin centre 74.73°S, 132.93°E, 316 km across, from the IAU Gazetteer of Planetary Nomenclature; the landing spot inside the basin is not yet published
